title: Can India Exploit China’s ‘Malacca Dilemma’?
author: Jahnavi Sodhi
text:
A true-color image of the Strait of Malacca acquired on August 22, 2025, by the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) on NASA’s Aqua satellite.
Credit: NASA
India faces one of the most challenging security environments in the world, confronting not one but two adversarial neighbors: Pakistan and China. While New Delhi retains the conventional military upper hand over Islamabad, in Beijing it confronts a militarily and economically superior power that has repeatedly used force to alter the status quo along their disputed border.Since the 1962 border war, India and China have faced a series of military confrontations, including the 2017 Doklam standoff and the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. More recently, Beijing reportedly provided Islamabad with critical intelligence support during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, raising the likelihood that any future Indo-Pak crisis will unfold against the backdrop of Chinese support for Islamabad.[...]
